q: can I give Motrin to my 8 month old for fever
text:
Yes — ibuprofen (Motrin) can be given to a child over 6 months old for fever, according to MedlinePlus [6]. Give it every 6 to 8 hours, and check the packaging or leaflet to be sure the medicine suits your child [3][6]. Know your child's weight before giving it [6].

The main goal is your child's comfort, not bringing the temperature itself down [5]. Keep them well hydrated, in a room that is not too warm, and don't overdress them [5]. If your baby is breastfed, keep breastfeeding as normal [3]. Paracetamol is another option, and both work about as well as each other [5].

Get medical advice if you're worried about your child, or if the medicine is not helping [3].

q: my son threw up twice this morning, what should I give him to drink
text:
Give him an oral rehydration solution, not water alone or a homemade mix. The main risk with vomiting is dehydration, so the priority is getting fluids in, according to the SEUP [1][3].

When he vomits, wait 20 minutes, then give oral rehydration solution — 2 to 5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour. Watch how well he takes it: if he keeps it down, you can slowly increase how often you offer it. Do not use homemade solutions like lemonade or commercial soft drinks [3].

You can buy oral rehydration solutions for children without a prescription; they replace both the fluids and the salts he is losing [5].

Get help if he is under 3 months and has vomited two or more feeds, if he vomits a lot and cannot keep down solids or liquids, if the vomit is green or contains blood or looks like coffee grounds, or if he is drowsy, limp, very thirsty, has sunken eyes, cries without tears or is passing little urine [7].

q: how do I know if my child is getting dehydrated from vomiting
text:
Vomiting is one of the causes of dehydration, which happens when the body loses more fluid than it takes in [1].

Offer fluids to replace what is lost. Oral rehydration fluids you can get over the counter are the most helpful for mild dehydration, according to the CDC [2]. After a vomit, wait 20 minutes, then give oral rehydration solution, 2–5 ml every 5 minutes for an hour, says the SEUP; if the child keeps it down, you can slowly increase how often you give it [5]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks [5].

Get help if the child is listless, vomits many times, or will not take fluids — consult your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3]. If you think the child is severely dehydrated, call your doctor [2].

q: my 5 year old has been coughing all night, what can I do
text:
A cough that keeps a child awake at night is common in preschool children, and viral respiratory infections are the main cause of wheezing at this age [2]. If your child has a cough that comes in fits, especially at night, and is otherwise well, that pattern can also be whooping cough, which starts like a cold with a mild occasional cough [1].

What to do now: keep the room calm and let your child rest propped up if that helps. If your child has been diagnosed with asthma, the SEUP says the bronchial obstruction typically improves with bronchodilator medicines such as salbutamol [2]; give it exactly as your doctor or the leaflet says, since the dose depends on your child's weight.

Get help if your child is breathing fast, the chest or ribs pull in with each breath, or the lips look blue — that means the oxygen in the blood is low [5].

q: my son has been coughing for a week after a cold
text:
A cough that lingers after a cold is common, and cold symptoms can last 10 to 14 days [6]. Whooping cough also starts like a cold, with a runny nose and mild, occasional cough, and after about a week it turns into coughing bouts that last for minutes and are worse at night, sometimes with a "whoop" sound between coughs [4]. Keep offering fluids and let him rest. If the cough is coming in fits, or he is struggling to breathe, vomiting with the coughing, or turning blue or grey, get medical care right away [1][4].

q: he has a cough but no fever and is eating normally
text:
A cough without fever, with normal eating, is usually nothing to worry about. A high temperature is the body's natural response to fighting infections like coughs and colds, according to the NHS [1].

Keep offering fluids and normal meals. There is no need to treat a fever that is not there, and no medicine is needed for a mild cough. If a fever does appear, do not undress your child or sponge them down to cool them, and do not give aspirin to children under 16 [1].

Get help if your child is under 3 months old and has a temperature of 38C (100.4 °F) or higher, is 3 to 6 months old and has a temperature of 39C (102.2 °F) or higher, has a rash along with a high temperature, has a high temperature lasting 5 days or more, is not eating or is not their usual self, or is dehydrated [1].

Red spots on the stomach that appear in a day are usually caused by a mild, self-limiting problem, and most children with them do not need urgent treatment [1]. q: my 6 year old fell from the bed and hit the back of his head
text:
Most head injuries in children are not serious, and most children recover quickly [2][6]. The usual symptoms after a knock to the head are headache, confusion, brief memory loss, dizziness, nausea, vomiting and drowsiness [1].

For the headache you can give ibuprofen or paracetamol in the dose your doctor indicates [6]. He can sleep, but after a more significant knock it is worth waking him every 4 hours [6]. Keep him resting physically and mentally for 24 to 48 hours, with no sport and no screens, then return to normal activities gradually [4]. No special diet is needed [6].

Watch over the first 24 hours for a severe or worsening headache, repeated vomiting, confusion or disorientation, behaviour changes, trouble speaking or walking, or blood or clear fluid from the nose or ears [3][4]. Get urgent medical help if he was knocked out, cannot stay awake, has a seizure, is vomiting, or is dizzy [2].

q: what foods should I start with for a baby who just turned 6 months
text:
At around 6 months, milk alone no longer meets all your baby's energy and nutrient needs, so solid foods are needed alongside it, according to the WHO [1]. Start with small amounts and increase them gradually as your baby grows, and build up the consistency and variety of foods step by step [1]. Give 2–3 meals a day at this age, and keep breastfeeding on demand [1].

At the beginning, how much your baby eats matters less than getting used to eating — most energy and nutrients still come from breast milk or first infant formula [2]. Offer one new food at a time so you can spot any allergic reaction, such as a rash, diarrhoea or vomiting, according to MedlinePlus [5]. Do not give honey before the first birthday, and avoid cow's milk, unpasteurised foods and choking hazards like whole nuts and grapes [5].

q: how much water can a 9 month old drink
text:
For a 9-month-old, breast milk or formula should stay the main drink, and water is offered in small amounts alongside meals rather than as a drink on its own. The SEUP advises increasing fluid intake, preferably water, to soften stools and make them easier to pass [6]. It does not give a specific amount for this age, so ask your paediatrician how much your baby should drink each day [1].

If your baby has diarrhoea or vomiting, the SEUP and the WHO both stress replacing lost fluids and electrolytes: oral rehydration solution is the treatment of choice, given in small sips, and breastfeeding should continue throughout [5]. Signs that mean your baby needs to be seen include vomiting many times and not tolerating solids or liquids, or blood in the stool [6].

q: my baby refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day
text: A baby who refuses vegetables but eats fruit all day is a common phase, and the AEP advises introducing the whole variety of fruits and vegetables gradually, at any daily meal, varying how they are offered — puréed, mashed or in small pieces [3]. Taste for different flavours, including bitter ones like some vegetables, is formed early, and early exposure to different tastes may reduce the risk of refusing new foods [3]. Keep offering vegetables alongside fruit without forcing, and give whole fruit rather than juice: fruit juices offer no nutritional benefit over whole fruit and can displace other foods [3]. If the child is constipated, the SEUP recommends more fluids, more fibre-rich meals with fruit and vegetables, and not replacing fruit with juice [5].

q: my daughter is 13 months and still mostly drinks formula
text:
At 13 months, formula alone is not enough: complementary feeding means giving solid or liquid foods other than breast milk or infant formula as a complement, not a substitute [2]. The WHO and UNICEF recommend starting complementary foods from 6 months while milk feeding continues up to 2 years or more [1].

Offer her a variety of suitable solid foods alongside her formula, and keep mealtimes based on her hunger and fullness cues [6]. A diet with enough variety and enough meals a day is what covers a young child's nutritional needs [1].

If you are unsure how to move her on from mostly formula, ask your doctor or health visitor for feeding advice — families with children under 2 should be able to get breastfeeding and feeding counselling [1].

q: how often should a newborn poop
text: How often a newborn poops varies a lot from baby to baby — the rhythm and consistency of stools differs from one person to another, and it is not essential that a baby has a bowel movement every day, according to the SEUP [3]. What matters more is the consistency: constipation is when stools become too hard, with discomfort or incomplete emptying, sometimes with fewer stools than usual [6]. For a baby under 6 months, keep the usual feeding — breast milk or formula [3]. Daily, it is worth noting down the baby's stools and urine so you can see the pattern [5]. q: my baby had a seizure last year and has a fever today
text:
A febrile seizure can happen when a child has a high temperature, and it is not usually serious or likely to harm your child or cause long-term effects, according to the NHS [3]. Fever itself usually settles within 1 to 4 days [1].

If your child has another seizure, do not move them or try to hold them in place, do not put anything in their mouth, and do not try to cool them by undressing them or sponging with cold water [5]. A febrile seizure usually lasts 2 to 3 minutes, and it is rare for one to last more than 10 minutes [2].

Get medical help if your child has a seizure lasting more than 5 minutes, has trouble breathing, has stiffness or twitching on only one side, is more sleepy than usual for more than an hour afterwards, or has more than one seizure within 24 hours [2]. After a first febrile seizure, your child needs to be checked in hospital [6].

q: when should I take my kid to the doctor for a sore throat
text:
Sore throats are very common and usually nothing to worry about — they normally get better by themselves within a week, according to the NHS [5]. Most are caused by viruses like a cold or flu [3].

To help soothe it: offer plenty of water, cool or soft foods, and rest, and avoid smoky places [5]. Paracetamol or ibuprofen can relieve the pain — check the leaflet or ask a pharmacist first, and never give a child aspirin [6][1]. Don't give young children small hard things to suck, like lozenges or hard sweets, because of the risk of choking [5].

See a doctor if your child is under 5 and needs help for the sore throat, or if it does not improve after a week [2]. Get urgent help if they have trouble breathing or can't swallow, are drooling, make a high-pitched sound when breathing, or are getting worse quickly [2].

White flakes on the scalp with itching are most often dandruff, a common skin condition that is not harmful and cannot be caught from anyone else [6]. It is not caused by poor hygiene, though it can be more noticeable if the hair is not washed regularly [1].

A bee sting is a common allergen, and most reactions are mild [1]. Watch the sting site for pain, redness or swelling, and keep an eye out for a raised, itchy rash or redness of the skin [7].

For a serious reaction, the signs to look for are swelling of the lips, mouth, throat or tongue, fast or struggling breathing, a tight throat or trouble swallowing, or skin, tongue or lips turning blue, grey or pale [7]. q: my baby has a temperature of 100.4, is that considered a fever
text:
100.4 °F = 38 °C.

If your baby is under 3 months old, a temperature of 100.4 °F (38 °C (100.4 °F)) needs a doctor the same day [5].

For an older baby, yes — 100.4 °F (38 °C (100.4 °F)) is considered a fever, according to the NHS [3]. A normal temperature in babies is about 36.4 °C (97.5 °F), and a high temperature is usually 38 °C (100.4 °F) or above [3]. Fever is very common in young children and usually settles within 1 to 4 days [1].

You can usually look after them at home: keep breastfeeding or offering plenty of fluids, watch for signs of dehydration, and check on them regularly, including during the night [2]. If they are distressed or uncomfortable, you can give paracetamol or ibuprofen — check the leaflet to be sure the medicine suits your child, and ask a pharmacist or doctor if you are unsure [2]. The right dose depends on your child's age and weight, so follow the leaflet or your doctor's advice.

Get medical advice if you are worried, or if the medicine is not helping [2].

q: can babies get dehydrated from breastfeeding
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Signs of dehydration: sunken eyes, little urine, dry mouth, persistent vomiting or heavy diarrhoea >24 h
text:
Breastfeeding does not cause dehydration — it protects against it. Breast milk is a fluid, and exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months is one of the key measures to prevent dehydration from diarrhoea, according to the WHO [5].

If your baby is unwell with vomiting or diarrhoea, keep breastfeeding normally, and even more often if they want it [3]. Offer smaller amounts more frequently to reduce the risk of vomiting [3]. If they need extra fluids, oral rehydration solution is the best choice — it replaces the water and salts lost [5]. Avoid sports drinks, sweets and juices, which have too much sugar and the wrong balance of salts for a child with diarrhoea [3].

If your baby is showing signs of dehydration, they need to be seen — oral rehydration solution is for mild dehydration, and severe dehydration may need fluids through a vein [2].

text:
If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day [2].

For an older child, cold hands and feet with a fever are part of how the body raises its temperature: the blood vessels near the skin narrow to keep heat in, according to the NHS [2]. A fever is the body's normal response to fighting an infection, and it is not an illness in itself [5].

What helps now: take the temperature with a thermometer, under the arm is fine [5]. Offer plenty of fluids [6]. Do not undress your child or sponge them down to cool them, and do not wrap them in too many clothes or bedclothes [2]. q: my son is 4 and weighs 25 pounds, is that too little
text:
25 lb = 11.3 kg.

Whether 25 pounds is too little for a 4-year-old depends on his height, not on the weight alone. The WHO growth standards for children under 5 use weight for height, and a child is considered underweight for their height only when that measure falls far below the median of the reference [1]. Health providers can pick up undernutrition or overweight early by following these growth patterns, before a child crosses a growth threshold [2].

What to do now: have his weight and height measured and plotted on the WHO growth chart for his age and sex, and ask your doctor to interpret the curve. The WHO recommends that every child has their own growth chart so their growth can be followed properly [4]. A single weight is not enough to judge — what matters is whether his curve follows a line close to the normal percentiles over time [5].

If you are worried, your doctor can assess his growth and tell you whether it is on track.

q: what should I know about malaria symptoms in a child returning from Africa
text: Malaria is a potentially fatal disease spread by mosquito bites, and children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection [1]. The first symptoms are usually fever, headache and chills, appearing about 10 to 15 days after the bite of an infected mosquito [2]. Because early symptoms look like many other febrile illnesses, it is easy to mistake them for something else, so testing as soon as possible matters [2]. Early treatment of a mild case can stop the infection getting worse [2]. Severe signs include extreme tiredness, altered consciousness, seizures, difficulty breathing, dark or bloody urine, yellowing of the eyes and skin, and abnormal bleeding; anyone with these needs emergency care quickly [2]. If your child becomes unwell after returning from Africa, get them tested for malaria without delay [2].

q: my daughter fainted for a few seconds at school and feels fine now
text:
A short faint like this is a syncope: a sudden, brief loss of consciousness that happens when not enough blood or oxygen reaches the brain, according to the SEUP [2]. It often follows heat, pain, fear, anxiety, standing still for a long time, or getting up suddenly [2].

What helps now: let her sit or lie down straight away if she feels unwell again, and breathe slowly and deeply [5]. If she faints, lay her down with her legs raised and her head to one side so she breathes better [5]. After resting, children usually recover quickly, within a couple of minutes [5]. She can get up slowly — sit first, then stand after a few minutes [5]. Encourage her to drink more fluids, especially with exercise [4].

Get urgent help if she takes more than 3–5 minutes to come round, if the faint happened during exercise or while sitting, or if it came with palpitations, chest pain, jerking of the limbs or passing urine [6].

q: mi hijo tiene fiebre despues de las vacunas
text:
Si el bebé tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico el mismo día.

En un niño mayor, la fiebre después de las vacunas es una reacción esperable: la inmunogenicidad y la seguridad de las vacunas son, en general, similares en prematuros y en nacidos a término, según la AEP [3]. No hay motivo para retrasar las vacunas del calendario: la norma general es mantenerlas sin demoras [2].

Lo que ayuda ahora: ofrécele líquidos con frecuencia y deja que descanse. Si tiene fiebre y malestar, puedes darle paracetamol o ibuprofeno; la dosis depende de su edad y su peso, así que consúltala con tu pediatra o en el prospecto. No hace falta dosis reducidas ni fraccionadas por haber sido prematuro: la dosis de cada vacuna es la misma que en un nacido a término [1].

Las edades de las vacunas siguen el calendario nacional de Estados Unidos.

¿Qué edad tiene? Con la edad afino la respuesta.

q: my 18 month old has a fever of 103 and won't take Tylenol
text:
103 °F = 39.4 °C.

A fever of 103 °F is high, and fever is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection [1]. The main goal is your child's comfort, not bringing the number down by itself [3].

Keep offering plenty of liquids in small amounts often, keep the room comfortably cool, and don't bundle them up or use cold baths or wet cloths — those are unpleasant and don't help [3]. It's normal for them to lose their appetite, so don't force food [3].

If they won't take Tylenol by mouth, ask your doctor or pharmacist about other ways to give it, since the right amount depends on your child's weight [4]. Acetaminophen can be given every 4 to 6 hours, and ibuprofen every 6 to 8 hours, but not to children under 6 months [4]. Never give aspirin to a child [4].

q: why does my 3 year old have a temperature of 105 degree celsius
text:
105 °F = 40.6 °C.

A temperature of 105 °C is not possible — that reading must be Fahrenheit, and 105 °F is about 40.5 °C (104.9 °F), a high fever. Fever is not an illness; it is usually a sign the body is fighting an infection, and most fevers in children are caused by infections [1]. Fever is a normal, good response to infection and does not mean the child is more seriously ill [5].

What to do now: check the temperature with a thermometer, under the arm is fine [5]. If there are no warning signs, start with physical measures — remove extra clothing, give fluids, reduce activity, and a lukewarm bath only if the child is comfortable [5]. If the child is uncomfortable, paracetamol or ibuprofen can be given; paracetamol is the first choice [4]. The dose depends on the child's weight.

Fever rarely goes above 40.5 °C (104.9 °F) on its own and does not rise endlessly [5].

q: my toddler has very hard poop and cries when he goes
text:
Hard, dry poop that hurts to pass is constipation, and in most cases it lasts a short time and is not serious [3]. The main sign is stool that is harder than usual, sometimes with pain or a feeling of not finishing [2][4].

What helps: offer more fluids, preferably water, to soften the stool and make it easier to pass [1]. Add more fibre — wholegrain cereals and bread, fruit and vegetables — and don't replace fruit with juice, which has little fibre [1]. Keep to a regular routine and don't hold in the urge to go [1]. Don't give laxatives or enemas without asking your doctor [1].

It's not important that he poops every day; the rhythm and consistency of stools vary from person to person [1][3].

See your doctor if the constipation comes with bad abdominal pain, blood in the stool, or repeated vomiting with refusal of food and fluids, according to the SEUP [1].

Offer plenty of fluids, and if the fever is above 38°C and your child is uncomfortable, give the antipyretic your paediatrician normally recommends [4]. q: my 5 year old complains of stomach ache and won't eat anything
text:
A stomach ache with no appetite is common in children, and the NHS says it can be part of constipation — especially if they have not had a poo at least 3 times in the last week, or the poo is dry, hard or lumpy, or they strain or feel pain when they go [6]. See a doctor if the stomach ache keeps coming back or they seem unwell in themselves.

बुखार के साथ दाने कई चीज़ों से हो सकते हैं। हैंड, फुट एंड माउथ डिज़ीज़ में पहले गले में दर्द, तेज़ बुखार और खाने में मन न लगना होता है, और कुछ दिन बाद मुँह में छाले तथा हाथ-पैरों पर उभरे दाने निकल आते हैं; ये अक्सर 7 से 10 दिन में खुद ठीक हो जाता है, NHS के अनुसार [3][1]। खुले दाने जो खुजली वाले हों, वे चिकनपॉक्स के हो सकते हैं, जिसमें बुखार और बेचैनी भी होती है [5]। खसरे में पहले ज़ुकाम जैसे लक्षण आते हैं और 3 से 5 दिन बाद चेहरे से शुरू होकर नीचे की ओर फैलने वाले लाल चकत्ते निकलते हैं [4]।

दानों को छूकर या दबाकर देखें: अगर दाने दबाने पर भी न मिटें, या बच्चा सुस्त लगे, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: मेरा 6 महीने का बच्चा दूध कम पी रहा है और पेशाब भी कम कर रहा है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text: ऊपर की चेतावनी में जो लिखा है, वह अभी कीजिए। इस ख़ास स्थिति पर मेरे दिशानिर्देशों में और जानकारी नहीं है, इसलिए मैं ऐसा कुछ नहीं जोड़ूँगा जिससे आपको देर हो।

missing: पानी की कमी (निर्जलीकरण) के घर पर देखने वाले लक्षण जैसे धँसी आँखें, सूखा मुँह, आँसू न आना, सुस्ती — जो बैनर में हैं पर पैसेज में नहीं
दस्त/उल्टी होने पर स्तनपान सामान्य रूप से और माँगने पर अधिक बार जारी रखने की सलाह (पैसेज 1)
बच्चे को भूखा न रखें, थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार खाना दें (पैसेज 1)
चीनी वाले पेय, जूस और स्पोर्ट्स ड्रिंक से बचें क्योंकि इनमें शक्कर ज़्यादा और इलेक्ट्रोलाइट असंतुलित होते हैं (पैसेज 1)
gap: 6 महीने के बच्चे में कम दूध पीना और कम पेशाब करना — इस उम्र के लिए मूत्र संक्रमण या निर्जलीकरण की जाँच और ORS/घरेलू तरल पदार्थ की सटीक मात्रा किसी पैसेज में नहीं है
भारत में आपातकालीन सेवा का नंबर या कहाँ जाना है, इसकी कोई जानकारी पैसेज में नहीं है
util.note: जवाब सही दिशा में है पर पैसेज में मौजूद व्यावहारिक सलाह (स्तनपान जारी रखना, थोड़ा-थोड़ा बार-बार देना, मीठे पेय से बचना) नहीं दी गई।

q: मेरी बेटी बिस्तर से गिर गई और उसके बाद एक बार उल्टी हुई
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: सिर पर चोट के बाद उल्टी
text: सिर की चोट के बाद उल्टी होना एक ऐसा लक्षण है जिसके लिए तुरंत आपातकालीन विभाग जाना चाहिए, SEUP के अनुसार [1]। अगर गिरना एक मीटर से अधिक ऊँचाई से हुआ था, या बच्चा तीन महीने से छोटा है, तो भी तुरंत अस्पताल ले जाना चाहिए [1]। रास्ते में बच्चे को आराम से लिटाए रखें और उल्टी होने पर उसे करवट पर लिटाएँ ताकि वह साँस ले सके। होश बनाए रखने के लिए उसे बार-बार बुलाते रहें और उसकी निगरानी करते रहें। अस्पताल में डॉक्टर ज़रूरी जाँच करेंगे और तय करेंगे कि आगे कोई परीक्षण चाहिए या नहीं [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Traumatismo craneal. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS

q: बच्चे को कब्ज है और पॉटी करते समय बहुत रोता है
text:
कब्ज़ शिशुओं में रोने के आम कारणों में से एक है, और कुछ शिशुओं में कब्ज़ कोलिक से भी जोड़ा जाता है [2][5]। शिशु को आराम देने की कोशिश करें और रोने के शांत होने का इंतज़ार करें [1]।

अगर रोना लगातार हो और शिशु को शांत या ध्यान भटकाकर चुप न कराया जा सके, या रोना उनके सामान्य रोने जैसा न लगे, तो यह बीमारी का संकेत हो सकता है — ऐसे में अपने डॉक्टर से संपर्क करें [4]। अगर शिशु को बुखार हो, उल्टी हो या मल में खून आए, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [6]।
sources: [1] NHS — "Soothing a crying baby" (2026), section "Colic", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/baby
[2] NHS — "Colic" (2022), section "Symptoms of colic", p. 1 — https://www.nhs.uk/condition
[4] NHS — "Soothing a crying baby" (2026), section "Crying and illness", p. 1 — https://ww
[5] SEUP — "Cólico del lactante. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿QUÉ SON LOS CÓ
[6] SEUP — "Cólico del lactante. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁNDO DEBEMOS

wrong: The answer frames the whole reply around colic and crying, while the parent's problem is constipation with pain on passing stool; the passages only mention constipation as one possible reason for crying, not how to manage it.

The answer says 'कब्ज़ शिशुओं में रोने के आम कारणों में से एक है' (constipation is a common cause of crying in babies) — passage [2] lists constipation only as one of several possible reasons to consider when unsure, not as a common cause.

The answer attributes the 'fever, vomiting or blood in stool' warning to the SEUP colic passage [6], but that passage is about when to go to an emergency department for colic episodes, not for constipation.
missing: Passage [2] advises that if you are not sure what is wrong, speak to your health visitor, call NHS 111 or see a GP — the answer only says contact a doctor in specific severe cases.
Passage [2] notes that crying may be due to a dirty nappy, hunger, wind or reflux, which should be checked before assuming colic.
Passage [6] lists additional reasons to seek urgent care: the child not returning to normal between crying episodes, pallor, sweating, lethargy or refusing feeds.
gap: No passage gives any advice on managing constipation in a baby (diet, fluids, when to treat, or how to relieve pain on passing stool).
No passage covers the age of the child, which matters for constipation advice.
util.note: La respuesta se centra en el cólico y el llanto, no en el estreñimiento ni en el dolor al hacer caca, que es lo que pregunta la madre.

q: मेरे बच्चे के हाथ पैर ठंडे हैं लेकिन शरीर गर्म है
text:
बुखार के दौरान हाथ-पैर ठंडे होना आम बात है: जब बुखार चढ़ रहा होता है तो बच्चे को ठंड लगती है, कभी-कभी कंपकंपी होती है और खासकर हाथों और पैरों की त्वचा पर जाल जैसा लाल रंग दिख सकता है, ऐसा SEUP कहता है [2]। जब बुखार उतरता है तो बच्चा पसीना-पसीना हो जाता है, लाल पड़ जाता है और उसे गर्मी लगती है [2]।

बुखार का मतलब है शरीर का तापमान 38°C से ऊपर, और यह शरीर के अपनी रक्षा करने का संकेत है — ज़्यादातर मामलों में इसकी वजह साधारण, अक्सर वायरल, संक्रमण होता है [4]। बुखार में भूख कम लगना, थकान या सिरदर्द होना भी सामान्य है [2]।

दवा के बारे में: बुखार बहुत तेज़ हो तो डॉक्टर पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन जैसी बिना पर्ची की दवा की सलाह दे सकते हैं, पर बच्चों को एस्पिरिन नहीं देनी चाहिए, और डिहाइड्रेशन से बचने के लिए पर्याप्त तरल पिलाना ज़रूरी है, MedlinePlus के मुताबिक [1]। खुराक बच्चे के वज़न पर निर्भर करती है।
sources: [1] MedlinePlus — "Fiebre", p. 1 — https://medlineplus.gov/spanish/fever.html
[2] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿CUÁLES SON LOS SÍNTOMAS?",
[4] SEUP — "Fiebre. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿QUÉ ES LA FIEBRE?", p. 1 —

missing: बुखार उतरते समय पसीना आना, लाल होना और गर्मी लगना सामान्य है (यह उत्तर में है, लेकिन ठंडे हाथ-पैर के साथ माता-पिता के लिए यह आश्वासन कम स्पष्ट है)
बुखार के दौरान कंपकंपी और त्वचा का जाल जैसा लाल होना (cutis marmorata) विशेष रूप से हाथ-पैरों पर सामान्य है — यह उत्तर में है
बुखार के साथ भूख कम लगना, थकान या सिरदर्द सामान्य है — यह उत्तर में है
gap: बुखार में हाथ-पैर ठंडे होने पर माता-पिता को क्या करना चाहिए (जैसे कंबल से न ढकना, हल्के कपड़े) — इस पर कोई मार्गदर्शन नहीं
किस उम्र के बच्चे में बुखार पर तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलना चाहिए — इस पर कोई मार्गदर्शन नहीं
बुखार के साथ खतरे के संकेत (जैसे सुस्ती, दौरा, सांस लेने में कठिनाई) — इस पर कोई मार्गदर्शन नहीं
util.note: उत्तर ठंडे हाथ-पैर के कारण और सामान्य लक्षण बताता है, पर माता-पिता को क्या करना चाहिए और कब डॉक्टर से मिलना चाहिए यह नहीं बताता।

q: मेरा बच्चा बहुत सुस्त है और ठीक से जाग नहीं रहा
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: जवाब नहीं दे रहा; बहुत ज़्यादा सुस्ती या चिड़चिड़ापन
text: बच्चे का सुस्त होना और ज़्यादा देर जागते न रहना निमोनिया की गंभीरता के संकेत हैं, ऐसा विकासपीडिया बताता है [2]। ऐसे में बच्चे को तुरंत अस्पताल ले जाना चाहिए [2]। रास्ते में बच्चे को खाने-पीने के लिए मजबूर न करें, और बुखार हो तो गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछ लें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं [2]।
sources: [2] Vikaspedia — "बच्चों को होने वाली आम बीमारियॉं — स्रोत: भारत स्वास्थ्य" (2020), sectio

wrong: The answer attributes the advice to Vikaspedia [2], but the passage [2] is about pneumonia severity signs; the emergency banner reason (not responding, extreme lethargy/irritability) is not what passage [2] describes.
The answer tells the parent to take the child to hospital, but the banner says to call 112 or go to emergency immediately; the answer omits the emergency call instruction.
missing: Passage [2] lists other severity signs: seizures with fever, child refusing to eat/drink or breastfeed, chest indrawing, grunting or whistling sounds, bluish tinge on skin/lips/nails/face.
Passage [2] says to seek medical help immediately on seeing ANY of these signs.
gap: No passage covers a child who is unresponsive or not waking properly outside the pneumonia context.
No passage gives guidance on what to do while waiting for emergency services (e.g., airway, breathing, position).
util.note: La respuesta se centra en neumonía y no menciona llamar al 112 ni otros signos de gravedad de los pasajes.

q: मेरे बच्चे ने आज बहुत कम पेशाब किया है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: पानी की कमी के लक्षण: आँखें धँसी, कम पेशाब, सूखा मुँह, लगातार उल्टी या 24 घंटे से ज़्यादा दस्त
text: बहुत कम पेशाब आना पानी की कमी का संकेत हो सकता है, और ऐसे में बच्चे को पानी जैसे तरल पदार्थ खूब देना चाहिए ताकि वह दिन में नियमित रूप से पेशाब करे और प्यासा न लगे [4]। अगर पेशाब गहरे रंग का या बदबूदार है, तो यह भी पानी की कमी से हो सकता है [3]। बच्चे को थोड़ी-थोड़ी मात्रा में बार-बार तरल देना आसान रहता है, और अगर दस्त या उल्टी हो रही हो तो मुँह से रिहाइड्रेशन घोल देना चाहिए [1]।
sources: [1] SEUP — "Gastroenteritis aguda. Información para padres" (2025), section "¿DEBEMOS OFRE
[3] NHS — "Urinary tract infections (UTIs)" (2025), section "Urinary tract infections (UTI
[4] NHS — "Urinary tract infections (UTIs)" (2025), section "How to prevent urinary tract

wrong: The answer treats reduced urination mainly as a UTI/prevention issue and cites passages about preventing UTIs and gastroenteritis, while the banner's dehydration warning (sunken eyes, dry mouth, persistent vomiting, >24h diarrhoea) is not addressed.
Passage [1] is about feeding during gastroenteritis and does not say to give oral rehydration solution for reduced urination; the answer attributes ORS advice to it.
Passage [4] is about preventing UTIs, not about treating dehydration; using it to support 'give plenty of fluids' for reduced peeing misapplies the source.
missing: The warning signs in the banner/passage [1] that mean go to emergency: vomiting a lot, not tolerating solids or liquids, vomiting even without taking anything.

q: mera baby raat ko bahut khans raha hai
text:
Raat ko khansi aksar asthma ka lakshan hoti hai. MedlinePlus ke mutabik bachchon mein asthma ki khansi khaas taur par raat ko ya subah jaldi hoti hai [3]. SEUP bhi kehta hai ki asthma mein khansi raat ko ho sakti hai [1].

Ghar par: kamre mein saaf humidifier ya thanda vaporizer lagaayein, aur bachche ko kaafi taraL peene ko dein [5]. Khansi ya sardi ke liye koi bhi dawa dene se pehle apne doctor ya pharmacist se poochhein, kyunki kuch cough-cold dawaiyon mein aise ingredients hote hain jo bachchon ke liye theek nahi [5]. Turant madad lein agar saans lene mein dikkat ya tez saans ho, hont ya chehra neela ya peela dikhe, ya khansi bahut tez ho [3]. SEUP ke mutabik agar saans ki takleef badhti jaaye — tez saans, pasliyan dikhna, pet zyada hilna — to turant doctor ke paas jaayein [7].

q: mere bete ke pairon par lal dane hain aur khujli ho rahi hai
text:
Aapke bete ke pairon par lal dane aur khujli heat rash (prickly heat) ho sakti hai — yeh takleef deti hai par aam taur par harmless hoti hai aur kuch dinon mein khud theek ho jati hai [6]. Iske lakshan hain chhote, ubhre hue dane, khujli ya chubhan wali feeling, aur halki sujan [6].

Ab kya karein: sabse zaroori hai skin ko thanda rakhna taaki pasina na aaye aur rash na bade [6]. Dheele cotton kapde pehnaayein, halki rajai use karein, thande paani se nahayein, aur paani zyada pilayein [6]. Khujli ke liye thandi cheez — geele kapde ya ice pack (towel mein lipta hua) — 20 minute tak lagayein, aur rash ko kharochne ke bajaye thap-thap karein [6]. Perfume wale shower gel ya cream use na karein [6].

Agar aap sure nahi hain ki yeh heat rash hai, to doosre rashes ke baare mein dekhein [6].

q: mere bete ko saans lene mein dikkat lag rahi hai
banner: 🚨 अभी 112 पर कॉल करें या तुरंत इमरजेंसी ले जाएँ। | कारण: साँस लेने में गंभीर दिक्कत (पसलियाँ दिखना, बहुत तेज़ साँस, साँस रुकना, नीलापन)
text:
Saans lene mein dikkat kai cheezon se ho sakti hai, aur inmein RSV, bronchiolitis, croup ya asthma shamil hain [2][3][5][6]. CDC ke mutabik RSV shuru mein halka ho sakta hai lekin kuch dinon mein gambhir ho jata hai, aur shuruaati lakshan naak behna, kam khana-peena aur khaansi hain jo aage chal kar saans lene mein dikkat ban sakte hain [2].

Abhi ke liye: apne bachche ko seedha aur aaram se rakhein, thoda utha kar god mein rakhein taaki saans lena aasan ho, aur chhote-chhote ghoont baar-baar de kar hydrated rakhein [5]. Agar bachcha doodh ya khana kam le raha hai to thoda-thoda aur baar-baar dein [5].

NHS ke mutabik bronchiolitis mein saans tez hona, wheezing ya crackling awaaz, aur doodh-peena mushkil hona aam hai, aur lakshan aksar din 3 se 5 ke beech sabse zyada hote hain [5]. Croup mein bhaunkne wali khaansi, awaaz baithna aur saans lene mein dikkat hoti hai [3].

Agar bachcha bahut thak gaya hai, irritable hai, ya doodh bilkul kam le raha hai to turant doctor se milna zaroori hai [5].

q: meri beti bahut sust hai aur jag nahi rahi

Aapki beti ki susti aur jag na paana gambhir lakshan ho sakte hain. q: mera bachcha bahut tez saans le raha hai

text:
तेज़ साँस लेना शिशुओं और छोटे बच्चों में ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस या RSV जैसी साँस की बीमारी का लक्षण हो सकता है — NHS के अनुसार ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस में बच्चा ज़्यादा तेज़ी से साँस लेता है और साँस लेने में तकलीफ़ होती है [3]। CDC के अनुसार RSV शुरू में हल्का लग सकता है, पर कुछ दिनों में गंभीर हो सकता है, और शुरुआती लक्षणों में नाक बहना, कम खाना-पीना और खाँसी शामिल हैं जो आगे चलकर घरघराहट या साँस लेने में कठिनाई बन सकती है [2]।

अभी बच्चे को आराम दें, थोड़ा-थोड़ा और बार-बार दूध या तरल दें ताकि वह डिहाइड्रेट न हो, और नाक बंद हो तो साफ़ करें [3]। WHO के अनुसार पाँच साल से छोटे बच्चों में खाँसी या साँस लेने में कठिनाई के साथ तेज़ साँस चलना निमोनिया का संकेत हो सकता है, और बहुत गंभीर हालत में बच्चा खाना-पीना बंद कर सकता है या बेहोश हो सकता है [6]।

अगर बच्चा दूध या पानी पीना बंद कर दे, पेशाब कम आने लगे, या बहुत सुस्त और चिड़चिड़ा लगे, तो तुरंत डॉक्टर से मिलें [3]।

q: my 2 year old has bad cough at night not sleeping
text:
A cough that is worse at night is common with colds and with croup, and croup symptoms are often worse at night [5]. Croup causes a barking cough that may sound like a seal, a hoarse voice, and a high-pitched rasping sound when breathing in [5].

If you think your child may have croup, ask your doctor for an urgent appointment — they may give medicine to shorten the illness [5]. Also get help if your child is getting worse or not getting better after seeing a doctor [5].

Keep the room calm and comfort your child; the sources do not describe other home measures for a night cough.

q: my 5 year old baby has red pimples on full body
text: A rash that spreads over the whole body can be caused by more than one illness, and the pattern matters. In measles, the rash usually starts on the face and upper neck and moves down over about three days to the chest, arms, legs and feet, and it usually lasts four to eight days before fading on its own, according to the WHO [4]. The first symptoms, lasting four to seven days, are fever, runny nose, cough, red watery eyes and tiny white spots inside the cheeks [4]. Measles spreads easily when an infected person breathes, coughs or sneezes [1]. There is no treatment for measles, but the MMR vaccine prevents it, according to MedlinePlus [2]. Chickenpox also causes a widespread itchy rash that turns into fluid-filled blisters and then scabs, often starting on the face, chest and back; calamine lotion and oatmeal baths can help the itch, and acetaminophen can help the fever — do not give aspirin [5].

q: my 6 year old child is not eating anything from 2 days
text:
A child who eats nothing for two days should be checked by a doctor, especially if they are also refusing to drink [1]. The SEUP says a child with marked refusal to eat or drink needs to be seen in an emergency department [1].

Offer fluids in small, frequent amounts: oral rehydration solutions contain water, sugar and salts in the right proportion to replace losses, and should be given in small doses often so they are tolerated [2]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace losses, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician [1].

Watch for signs of dehydration: much thirst, crying without tears, passing little urine or sunken eyes [1]. Also get help if the child is very irritable, drowsy or less responsive [1].

q: my 6 month old baby has congested chest and making whistling noise
banner: 🚨 With these symptoms your child should be seen in the emergency department today, without waiting. | Reason: Breathing difficulty: fast breathing, wheezing, ribs pulling in
text:
A whistling or wheezing chest in a 6-month-old is most often caused by a viral infection of the small airways, and in preschool children viral respiratory infections are the main cause of wheezing [3]. Bronchiolitis is one such infection: it affects the small bronchi, is caused by viruses (most often respiratory syncytial virus), and mostly affects children under 2 [4].

Keep feeding them and watch their breathing, how well they take their feeds, their colour and their general state [5]. There is no medicine that cures bronchiolitis; most cases improve over about 2 weeks, though the cough can last longer [5]. Sleeping semi-upright can help [5].

While you are on your way, keep them upright and comfortable, and keep offering feeds.

Get help today if they are breathing fast, their ribs are pulling in or their chest is dipping, or they are finding it hard to feed, according to the SEUP [6].

q: bukhar (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
6 महीने के बच्चे में तेज़ बुखार आम बात है और आमतौर पर 1 से 4 दिनों में तापमान सामान्य हो जाता है [1]। 38°C या उससे ज़्यादा तापमान बुखार माना जाता है [1]।

अभी यह करें: बच्चे को खूब तरल दें — अगर स्तनपान करता है तो सामान्य रूप से स्तनपान जारी रखें, निर्जलीकरण के संकेतों पर नज़र रखें, और भूख लगे तो खाना दें [3]। रात में भी नियमित रूप से बच्चे को देखते रहें [3]। बच्चे को घर पर ही रखें [3]। अगर बच्चा परेशान या असहज लगे तो पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन दें — पैकेजिंग या पर्ची देखकर पक्का करें कि दवा आपके बच्चे के लिए उपयुक्त है [3]। 3 महीने से कम उम्र के बच्चे को आइबुप्रोफेन न दें, और 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले बच्चे को भी नहीं [2]। बच्चे को एस्पिरिन न दें [2]।

अगर आप चिंतित हैं या पैरासिटामोल या आइबुप्रोफेन से आराम नहीं मिल रहा, तो डॉक्टर से सलाह लें [3]।

ध्यान दें: WHO के विकास चार्ट के अनुसार 6 महीने के बच्चे के लिए 5 किग्रा बहुत कम वज़न है। अगर वज़न सही है तो जल्द ही डॉक्टर से बच्चे की बढ़त जँचवाएँ; अगर लिखने में गलती हुई है तो उसे ठीक करें, क्योंकि दवा की खुराक वज़न से तय होती है।

q: क्या बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहला सकती हूँ? (उम्र: 6 महीने) (वज़न: 5 किलो)
text:
नहीं, बुखार उतारने के लिए बच्चे को नहलाएँ या स्पंज न करें — NHS के अनुसार बुखार शरीर की संक्रमण से लड़ने की स्वाभाविक और स्वस्थ प्रतिक्रिया है, इसलिए बच्चे के कपड़े न उतारें और न ही उसे ठंडा करने के लिए पानी से पोंछें [7]। साथ ही बच्चे को ज़्यादा कपड़ों या रज़ाई में न लपेटें [7]।

बुखार उतारने के लिए भारत स्वास्थ्य के अनुसार गुनगुने पानी में कपड़ा भिगोकर पूरा शरीर पोंछ लें, सिर्फ माथा नहीं [3]। बच्चे का खान-पान चालू रखने की कोशिश करें [3]।

6 महीने के बच्चे का वज़न 5 किलो है, और NHS के अनुसार 5 किलो से कम वज़न वाले बच्चे को इबुप्रोफेन न दें [7]। पैरासिटामोल की खुराक बच्चे के वज़न के अनुसार तय होती है [7]।

अगर बच्चे को दौरा पड़े, बच्चा खाने-पीने या स्तनपान से मना करे, सुस्त हो जाए, साँस लेते समय पसलियाँ अंदर खिंचें, सीने से कराहने या सींटी जैसी आवाज़ आए, या त्वचा, होंठ, नाखून व चेहरे पर नीली झलक दिखे, तो तुरंत चिकित्सीय सहायता लें [3]।

q: 3 साल के बच्चे को सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी की आवाज आ रही है
banner: 🚨 इन लक्षणों के साथ बच्चे को आज ही इमरजेंसी में दिखाना चाहिए, देर न करें। | कारण: साँस की दिक्कत: तेज़ साँस, सीटी जैसी आवाज़, पसलियाँ दिखना
text:
3 साल के बच्चे में सूखी खांसी और छाती से सीटी जैसी आवाज़ (सिबिलेंस) ब्रोंकियल रुकावट के कारण हो सकती है, और यह रुकावट सालबुटामोल जैसी ब्रोंकोडाइलेटर दवाओं से ठीक होती है [2]। प्रीस्कूल उम्र के बच्चों में सिबिलेंस का सबसे आम कारण सांस की वायरल इंफेक्शन है [2]। ऐसे लक्षण अस्थमा, ब्रोंकियोलाइटिस या छाती के इंफेक्शन में भी दिख सकते हैं [3][6]।

अभी बच्चे को आराम से, सीधा बैठाकर रखें और शांत रखें। दवा के बारे में अपने डॉक्टर से पूछें — सालबुटामोल की खुराक वही होगी जो डॉक्टर या दवा के पर्चे पर लिखी है [2]।

अगर बच्चा ठीक न हो रहा हो या हालत बिगड़ रही हो, तो डॉक्टर से मिलें [3]।

q: मेरे 5 साल के बच्चे के शरीर पर लाल दाने हो गए हैं और खुजली है
text:
5 साल के बच्चे में खुजली वाले छोटे लाल दाने स्केबीज़ (खाज) के कारण हो सकते हैं — यह छोटे कीड़ों (माइट्स) से होता है जो त्वचा में घुसकर अंडे देते हैं और तेज़ खुजली व दाने पैदा करते हैं [2]। अक्सर उंगलियों के बीच एक सिरे पर बिंदु वाली उभरी लकीरें दिखती हैं, और स्केबीज़ का इलाज आमतौर पर घर पर ही हो सकता है [4]।

इलाज क्रीम या मुँह से ली जाने वाली दवा से होता है [2]। इलाज शुरू करने के 24 घंटे तक दूसरों से नज़दीकी संपर्क से बचें; 5 साल या उससे बड़े बच्चे इलाज शुरू करते ही स्कूल जा सकते हैं [1]। इलाज कीड़ों को जल्दी मार देता है, पर खुजली कुछ हफ़्ते तक बनी रह सकती है [1]। खुजाने से त्वचा में संक्रमण (जैसे इम्पेटिगो) हो सकता है, इसलिए नाखून छोटे रखें [1]।

डॉक्टर से मिलें अगर फार्मेसी का इलाज पूरा होने के 2 से 4 हफ़्ते बाद भी खुजली बनी रहे, या त्वचा में संक्रमण लगे [1]।

q: क्या एमएमआर वैक्सीन बच्चे के लिए सुरक्षित है
text:
हाँ, एमएमआर वैक्सीन सुरक्षित है। विकासपीडिया के अनुसार लगभग सभी वैक्सीन्स के थोड़े-बहुत मामूली दुष्प्रभाव हो सकते हैं, लेकिन ये सारे टीके काफी सुरक्षित हैं और मामूली उपचार से ठीक हो जाते हैं [6]। दुष्प्रभाव होना यह संकेत है कि वैक्सीन असर दिखा रही है [6]।

nidirect के अनुसार टीके सुरक्षित, प्रभावी हैं और जान बचा सकते हैं [4]। बच्चों को तय समय पर टीके लगवाना ज़रूरी है, और अगर कोई टीका छूट जाए तो डॉक्टर से मिलकर उसे पूरा करवाएँ [4]।

भारत में एमएमआर सहित टीकों की उम्र और खुराक राष्ट्रीय टीकाकरण कार्यक्रम के अनुसार तय होती है, इसलिए अपने बच्चे के टीकाकरण की जानकारी अपने डॉक्टर या स्वास्थ्य कार्यकर्ता से लें [4]।

q: 3 saal ke bacche ko raat ko bahut khansi aati hai
text:
Raat ki khansi bachchon mein asthma ka ek aam lakshan hai — khaas taur par raat mein ya subah jaldi [1]. WHO ke mutabiq bhi khansi raat mein badh jaati hai [6].

Agar bachche ko saans lene mein takleef, seene mein jakadan, ya saans chhodte waqt seeti jaisi aawaz ho, to yeh bhi asthma ke lakshan ho sakte hain [1]. SEUP ke mutabiq khansi raat mein hone ke saath saans phoolna aur ghabrahat bhi ho sakti hai [2].

Dhyan rakhein: agar khansi bahut tez ho, saans lene mein sakht dikkat ho, ya chehre, hothon ya naakhunon ka rang neela ya peela pad jaye, to turant doctor se milna zaroori hai [1]. SEUP ke mutabiq hothon ke aas-paas neela rang oxygen kam hone ka sanket hai [2].

Asthma ke lakshan dikhne par doctor se salah lena chahiye [6].

[6] WHO — "Asma", section "Síntomas", p. 1 — https://www.who.int/es/news-room/fact-sheets/

q: mera 8 month ka baby bed se gir gaya aur ro raha hai
text:
Aapke 8 mahine ke baby ko bed se girne ke baad sar par chot lagi hai. SEUP ke mutabik sar par chot ke aam lakshan sir dard, uljhan, thodi der ke liye yaad na rehna, chakkar, ji michalna, ulti aur neend aana hain [1].

Ghar par 24 se 48 ghante aaram karayein — koi khel-kood ya screen (tablet, video game, smartphone) nahi [2]. Agar sir dard ho to ibuprofen ya paracetamol us dose mein dein jo aapke doctor ne batayi ho [6]. Khana-peena pehle jaisa hi chalega, bhookh ke hisaab se [6]. Zyada chot ke maamle mein har 4 ghante mein jagakar check karna theek hai [6].

Turant emergency le jaayein agar: tez ya badhta sir dard jo dawa se bhi kam na ho, baar-baar ulti, uljhan ya confusion, bahut chidchidapan ya jagane par mushkil se uthna, bolne ya chalne mein dikkat, ya naak/kann se khoon ya saaf paani aaye [2][5]. 8 mahine ke bachche mein yeh chot 3 mahine se zyada umar ki hai, lekin agar aapko uski halat ki fikar ho to bina der kiye dikhayein [5].

q: 5 saal ke child ko body pe red rashes ho gaye hain
text:
5 saal ke bachche par red rashes ke kai kaaran ho sakte hain, aur inme se kuch aam hain. WHO ke mutabik sarna (scabies) me tez khujli hoti hai, khaas taur par raat me, aur ungliyon, kalaiyon, baahon, pairon aur kamar ke aas-paas dane aur lakeerein dikhti hain; chhote bachchon me hatheli, talwe aur sar ki twacha par bhi zyada rash ho sakta hai [2]. MedlinePlus ke mutabik eccema se twacha sookhi ho jaati hai, khujli hoti hai aur kohni ke andar, ghutnon ke peeche, chehre, haathon aur pairon par sarpulli nikal aati hai [6].

Ghar par twacha ko narm rakhein aur khujli kam karne ke liye khaas soap, kapde aur lotion se bachein jo twacha ko chubhte hain [6]. Agar rash ke saath saans tez chal rahi ho, saans lene me dikkat ho, hoth ya zubaan soojh jaayein, ya bachcha sust ya kam jawab de raha ho, to turant local emergency number par call karein ya emergency department le jaayein [7].

q: kya polio ki drop dena zaroori hai
text:
Polio ki drop dena zaroori hai: polio vaccine (VPI) bachchon ke niyamit teekakaran ka hissa hai [3]. Spain ke Ministry of Sanidad ke teekakaran ke anusar, DTPa/VPI ki dose 2, 4 aur 11 mahine ki umar mein di jaati hai, aur 6 saal ki umar par ek booster [3]. CAV-AEP kehta hai ki jokhim wale naye sharirik shishuon mein bhi teekakaran bina deri shuru karna chahiye [2].

Agar aapke bachche ki koi dose chhoot gayi hai, to apne doctor se milein taaki pending dose poori ho sake [1].

q: my baby has diarrhea after we came back from a trip
text: Diarrhoea is usually a sign of an infection in the gut, and it can be caused by contaminated food or water or passed from person to person through poor hygiene, according to the WHO [6]. It should be treated with an oral rehydration salts solution — a mix of clean water, salt and sugar — and zinc supplements, which shorten the episode by about 25% and reduce stool volume by about 30% [1][4]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for the diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3]. See a health professional for persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration [1]. Signs to watch for include much thirst, crying without tears, little urine, sunken eyes, marked irritability or drowsiness, refusing to eat or drink, or persistent or intense abdominal pain [3].

q: क्या टीका लगने के बाद बुखार आना सामान्य है?
text:
अगर बच्चा 3 महीने से छोटा है, तो बुखार होने पर उसी दिन डॉक्टर को दिखाना ज़रूरी है।

बड़े बच्चों में टीके के बाद हल्का बुखार आना सामान्य है और चिंता की बात नहीं है। डी.पी.टी. या डी.टी. का टीका लगने के कुछ घंटों बाद बच्चे को हल्का बुखार हो सकता है, और ये दुष्प्रभाव आम तौर पर 2-3 दिनों में अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]। खसरे के टीके के 6-7 दिनों बाद भी हल्का बुखार और शरीर पर हल्के लाल दाने हो सकते हैं; इनके लिए इलाज की ज़रूरत नहीं, ये अपने आप ठीक हो जाते हैं [5]।

टीके के एक-दो घंटे बाद बच्चे को पेरासिटामॉल की गोली या शर्बत दी जा सकती है, पर खुराक के बारे में टीका लगाने वाले स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी की सलाह मानें — खुराक बच्चे की उम्र और वज़न पर निर्भर करती है [5]।

अगर लक्षण 2-3 दिनों में ठीक न हों, या इंजेक्शन की जगह लाल, गर्म या सूज जाए, तो शीघ्र ही किसी स्वास्थ्य कर्मचारी से परामर्श करें [5]।

बच्चे की उम्र कितनी है? उम्र जानकर मैं जवाब और सटीक कर सकता हूँ।

q: my child has been in the sun and now feels dizzy
text:
Heat illness happens when a child is out in the heat too long and the body can't cool itself, according to MedlinePlus [3]. Dizziness is one of the signs of heat stroke, along with dry skin, a fast strong pulse, nausea and confusion [3].

Do this now: move your child to a cool, shaded place, take off extra clothing, put cool wet cloths on the forehead, neck and armpits, offer cool water in small sips, and use a fan to bring the temperature down [6]. Do not give fever medicine for heat illness — physical cooling measures are used instead [5].

Get help at the emergency department if there is loss of consciousness or a seizure, confusion or trouble speaking or moving, vomiting that won't stop so they can't drink, or a fever above 39°C that doesn't come down with home measures [7].

q: solids baby ko kab se dena shuru kare
text:
Solid foods baby ko taqreeban 6 mahine ki umar se shuru karni chahiye, NHS ke mutabiq [2]. Shuru mein yeh zyada zaroori nahi ke baby kitna khata hai — ahem yeh hai ke woh khane ki aadat se waqif ho jaye; zyada tar energy aur nutrients abhi bhi doodh ya first infant formula se milte rahenge [2].

Dhire dhire miqdar aur variety barhate jayen, yahan tak ke baby ghar ke baqi logon ka khana chhote hisson mein kha sake [2]. Agar baby waqt se pehle paida hua tha, to solid foods kab shuru karni hain is par apne doctor ya health worker se mashwara karein [2].

Khilate waqt baby ko seedha aur safely baithayen, safety harness istemal karein, aur unhein akela nahi chhorna chahiye [6]. 6 mahine se cup se pani ke chhote ghoont dena shuru karein [6].

q: my child has loose motions since morning what should I give
text: Loose stools like this are usually gastroenteritis, which is usually not serious but can lead to dehydration [2]. Give your child an oral rehydration solution to replace the fluids and electrolytes lost [1]. Offer it in small amounts often, and keep breastfeeding normally, more often if your child wants it [6]. Keep giving a practically normal diet, just in smaller and more frequent portions, avoiding fatty foods, sweets and juices [6]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks, and do not give medicines to stop the diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your doctor [4]. Contact a health care provider right away if your child has a change in mental state such as irritability or lack of energy, diarrhoea lasting more than a day, any fever in an infant, frequent loose stools, vomiting often, severe belly pain, signs of dehydration such as thirst, dry mouth, urinating less than usual or no wet nappies for 3 hours or more, or stools that are black and tarry or contain blood or pus [2].

q: is MMR vaccine safe for my daughter
text:
The MMR vaccine is safe and effective: protection starts within 2 weeks of having it, and after 2 doses around 99% of people are protected against measles and rubella and around 88% against mumps, according to the NHS [2]. If someone does get mumps after being vaccinated, the symptoms are usually much milder [2].

For children who were born prematurely, there is no reason to think they respond differently to the vaccines given in the second year of life, and live vaccines such as MMR can be given when they are indicated, according to the AEP [1][4]. In general they need no special precautions [4].

The ages at which MMR is offered follow India's national immunisation schedule, so check the timing with your doctor.

q: my 6 month old has started solids, can I give banana
text: Yes, banana is a good first food. Soft fruit like banana is listed among the finger foods you can offer from around 6 months, according to the NHS [5]. Cut it into pieces big enough for your baby to hold in their fist with a bit sticking out — about the size of your own finger — and let them feed themselves [5]. Offer finger foods at each meal and let them explore, and avoid hard foods like whole nuts or raw carrot and apple, which are a choking risk [5].

q: my 5 year old has stomach pain and constipation
text:
Stomach ache is a common symptom in children and most causes are mild and get better on their own, such as constipation, gas or a tummy bug, according to the SEUP [2]. Constipation often causes a stomach ache and bloating too [1].

q: my 3 year old has malaria fever or maybe teething, how can I tell
text: Malaria and teething cannot be told apart from the fever alone: the first symptoms of malaria are often mild and similar to many other illnesses with fever, so it is hard to recognise as malaria [1]. The most common early symptoms are fever, headache and chills [1]. Malaria is a life-threatening disease spread by mosquito bites, mostly in tropical countries, and it does not pass from person to person [1]. Children under 5 are at higher risk of severe infection [1]. If you are in or have travelled to an area where malaria is common, take steps to prevent mosquito bites, which bite mainly between dusk and dawn [2]. If your child has a fever and could have been exposed to malaria, have them seen by your doctor.

q: my child has been scratching small bumps on his body
text: Small, itchy raised spots like these are often heat rash, which is uncomfortable but usually harmless and gets better on its own after a few days, according to the NHS [4]. The main thing is to keep the skin cool so it does not sweat and irritate the rash: loose cotton clothing, lightweight bedding, cool baths or showers, and plenty to drink [4]. To calm the itching, apply something cold such as a damp cloth or an ice pack wrapped in a tea towel for up to 20 minutes, and pat or tap the rash instead of scratching it [4]. Avoid perfumed shower gels or creams [4]. If the spots are instead raised bumps or patches that itch, sting or burn and can appear anywhere on the body, that fits hives, and a pharmacist can advise about antihistamine treatment, though it may not be suitable for young children [6][7].

q: what food to give 6 month baby for first time
text: Around 6 months, milk alone no longer meets all your baby's energy and nutrient needs, so solid foods are introduced alongside it, according to the WHO [3]. Start with small amounts — just a few pieces or teaspoons — and increase gradually as your baby grows [1][3]. q: my 4 year old has severe cough and catarrh
text:
A severe cough with catarrh (a runny nose) can be the first phase of whooping cough, which often starts like a cold with a runny nose, red watery eyes, sneezing and a mild or occasional cough, according to the Government of Canada [4]. This first phase usually lasts 1 to 2 weeks, and the cough then becomes more severe, with coughing fits that can make it hard to breathe [4].

If whooping cough is diagnosed within 3 weeks of the cough starting, antibiotics are given to help stop it spreading to others, though they may not reduce the symptoms, according to the NHS [6]. Hospital treatment is usually needed for severe whooping cough [6].

See your doctor if your child has severe coughing fits, trouble breathing, or vomiting after coughing, or if the cough is getting worse rather than better [4].

q: my 3 year old has watery stool and weakness
text:
Watery stools with weakness in a 3-year-old is usually gastroenteritis, which is usually not serious [3]. Give oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar — in small amounts, and zinc supplements, which shorten the diarrhoea by about 25% [1][4]. Keep offering nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or fizzy drinks to replace the losses [2], and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without asking your paediatrician [2].

Get help if your child is very thirsty, cries without tears, urinates little or has sunken eyes; is very irritable, drowsy or less responsive; cannot drink as fast as they lose fluid; refuses to eat or drink; has persistent or severe belly pain, or stools with a lot of blood [2].

q: what can I give my 2 year old for diarrhoea
text:
For a 2-year-old with diarrhoea, the main treatment is oral rehydration salts (ORS) — a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools, according to the WHO [1]. q: my baby is not passing urine as much as usual
text:
A baby who is not passing urine as much as usual may be dehydrated. In babies and small children, signs of dehydration include a dry mouth and tongue, crying without tears, not wetting nappies for 3 hours or more, high fever, unusual sleepiness, irritability and sunken eyes, according to MedlinePlus [5]. A child with diarrhoea is dehydrated when they are very thirsty, cry without tears, pass little urine, or have sunken eyes, according to the SEUP [2]. Marked irritability, drowsiness or a reduced response are also signs [2].

q: my daughter has small red spots after fever

If your child is under 3 months old, a fever needs a doctor the same day.

q: what solids to give first to 6 month baby

q: my 3 year old has fever 102, can I give Calpol
text:
102 °F = 38.9 °C.

Yes, you can give Calpol (paracetamol) — it helps when a child is distressed or uncomfortable because of a high temperature [3]. The aim is to ease their discomfort, not to bring the fever itself down [2].

Give it at the dose recommended by your doctor, every 6 to 8 hours [2]. Paracetamol and ibuprofen work about equally well, and alternating them routinely every 3 to 4 hours is not recommended [2]. Make sure your child drinks plenty of fluids, keep the room at a neutral temperature and don't over-wrap them [2]. Don't sponge them with cold water or wet cloths — it's unpleasant and doesn't work [2]. It's normal for them not to want food; don't force it, but keep offering drinks [2]. Children with a fever should not take aspirin [1].

q: can I give ORS to my 1 year old after diarrhea
text: Yes, you can give oral rehydration salts (ORS) to your 1-year-old after diarrhoea. The WHO lists rehydration with ORS as a key treatment for diarrhoea, and ORS is a mixture of clean water, salt and sugar that replaces the water and electrolytes lost in the stools [1]. Zinc supplements are also part of the treatment: they reduce how long the diarrhoea lasts by 25% and cut stool volume by about 30% [1]. Keep giving nutrient-rich foods, including breast milk, during the episode [1]. Do not use homemade solutions or commercial soft drinks to replace the losses, and do not give medicines for diarrhoea or vomiting without checking with your paediatrician, according to the SEUP [3]. See a health professional for persistent diarrhoea, blood in the stool, or signs of dehydration [1].

q: le ha salido un sarpullido rojo por las piernas y le pica
text:
Un sarpullido rojo que pica mucho en las piernas puede ser urticaria: ronchas o placas rojas y elevadas que aparecen en una zona y desaparecen de otras, y en la infancia la mayoría están causadas por una infección, según la SEUP [3]. También puede tratarse de una reacción alérgica, que además del sarpullido puede dar picazón, hinchazón o asma [4], o de una alergia alimentaria, cuyos síntomas suelen empezar entre unos minutos y dos horas después de comer el alimento [5].

Si sospechas que fue un alimento, evita dárselo y consulta con tu médico. Las alergias se diagnostican con pruebas de piel y sangre, y el tratamiento incluye medicinas y evitar la sustancia que la causa [4].

Busca atención urgente si tiene problemas para respirar, hinchazón de la cara, la lengua o los labios, o se marea o desmaya: puede ser una reacción grave [5].

El eccema causa sequedad y comezón con sarpullido, y rascarse empeora el enrojecimiento y la picazón (MedlinePlus [1]).

q: mi hijo tiene conjuntivitis y se le pegan los ojos al despertarse
text:
La conjuntivitis es el nombre médico de la conjuntivitis, y puede causar hinchazón, picor, escozor, secreción y enrojecimiento; en la mayoría de los casos se cura sin atención médica, según MedlinePlus [3]. Los ojos que se pegan al despertar son esa secreción, y la conjuntivitis bacteriana necesita tratamiento con gotas o pomada antibiótica [3].

Ahora limpia los párpados con agua tibia y una gasa limpia, sin frotar, y lávate las manos antes y después; la conjuntivitis infecciosa se contagia con facilidad de una persona a otra [3]. No hace falta que el niño se quede en casa ni falte al colegio, salvo que se encuentre muy mal [4].

Consulta a tu médico si la conjuntivitis no se ha resuelto en 7 días, o antes si hay dolor en los ojos, sensibilidad a la luz, cambios en la visión o los ojos muy rojos, según el NHS [4].

q: se le marcan las costillas al respirar pero luego se pone a jugar
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Dificultad para respirar grave (se marcan las costillas, respira muy rápido, pausas en la respiración, color azulado); Dificultad para respirar: respira rápido, «pitido» al respirar, se marcan las costillas
text:
Las costillas que se marcan al respirar son un signo de dificultad respiratoria, y la SEUP indica que en ese caso hay que acudir a urgencias [4]. Mientras llega la ayuda, mantén al niño incorporado y tranquilo, sin forzarlo a comer, y ofrécele sorbos pequeños de líquido si lo acepta [4].

Aunque después se ponga a jugar, el que las costillas se marquen sigue siendo un signo de dificultad para respirar, y la SEUP recomienda consultar en urgencias cuando aparece [2][4]. No esperes a que empeore ni a que aparezcan otros síntomas: el tiraje ya es motivo de consulta [4][5].

Si además tiene tos o mocos, puede tratarse de un catarro o una bronquiolitis, que a veces cursa con las costillas marcadas [3]. En cualquier caso, con dificultad respiratoria la SEUP recomienda acudir a urgencias para descartar complicaciones [4].

q: mi hijo tiene fiebre y rigidez en el cuello
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Rigidez de nuca: hay que descartar una meningitis ahora mismo
text:
Si el niño tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico el mismo día.

La meningitis puede agravarse muy rápido, y la fiebre con rigidez en el cuello es uno de los signos por los que hay que buscar atención médica de inmediato, según MedlinePlus [7]. Mientras llega la ayuda, no le des nada de comer ni de beber por si empeora, y mantenlo acompañado y vigilado [7].

Los exámenes para diagnosticar meningitis incluyen análisis de sangre, pruebas de imágenes y una punción espinal para examinar el líquido cefalorraquídeo; los antibióticos pueden tratar la meningitis bacteriana y las antivirales ayudan en algunos tipos de meningitis viral [7].

q: mi hija se ha caido de un segundo piso pero parece estar bien
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Caída por las escaleras o de más de un metro, o llanto que no se calma tras un golpe: que lo vea un médico hoy
text:
Un golpe en la cabeza es un traumatismo craneal, y los síntomas más habituales son dolor de cabeza, confusión, pérdida de memoria transitoria, mareo, náuseas, vómitos y somnolencia [1]. Como la caída fue desde más de un metro de altura, la SEUP recomienda consultar en urgencias [3].

Mientras la ven, no la dejen sola y permanezcan atentos a su comportamiento [3]. Es importante vigilarla durante las primeras 24 horas para detectar síntomas de gravedad [2]: dolor de cabeza intenso o que no mejora con paracetamol o ibuprofeno, vómitos repetidos, desorientación o confusión, irritabilidad o dificultad para despertarla si es muy pequeña, cambios en su comportamiento habitual, dificultad para hablar o caminar, o salida de sangre o líquido claro por la nariz o los oídos [6]. El personal médico hará las exploraciones necesarias y valorará si hacen falta pruebas adicionales [3].

q: mi bebe tiene 9 meses y todavia no tiene dientes
text:
La erupción de los dientes de leche empieza alrededor de los 6 meses, con los incisivos centrales inferiores, y sigue la secuencia habitual, según el Manual de Pediatría de la PUC Chile [6]. Que a los 9 meses todavía no le hayan salido no significa por sí solo que haya un problema: cada bebé lleva su propio ritmo.

Mientras tanto, puedes revisarle la boca con calma: mira los labios, la mucosa de las mejillas, las encías y la lengua, y aprovecha para empezar los cuidados de higiene oral [6]. Si te preocupa que no le salga ningún diente, coméntalo en su próxima revisión con tu pediatra, que podrá examinarle la boca y valorar si hay algún problema de oclusión o de otra índole [6].

q: mi hija ha dejado de decir palabras que antes decía
text: Perder palabras que antes decía es una señal para actuar pronto: si tu hija ha perdido habilidades que ya tenía, no esperes, habla con su médico y pide una evaluación del desarrollo, según los CDC [3]. Los CDC recomiendan que los niños se evalúen con herramientas estandarizadas a los 9, 18 y 30 meses, y para autismo a los 18 y 24 meses, o antes siempre que un padre o el médico tenga una preocupación [3]. Si tú o el médico siguen preocupados, pide una derivación a un especialista que valore a tu niña más a fondo [3]. Cuanto antes empiecen los servicios de desarrollo —como terapia del habla—, mejor es el resultado, según MedlinePlus [5]. Tú conoces mejor que nadie a tu hija [3].

q: mi hijo de 15 años tiene dolor en el pecho despues de hacer deporte
text:
El dolor de pecho tiene muchas causas y, en la mayoría de los casos, no se debe a un problema del corazón [1]. Cuando aparece después de hacer ejercicio o de una lesión en el pecho, puede tratarse de un esguince o distensión muscular: suele empeorar al respirar hondo y mejora con el reposo [1]. También puede aparecer con la ansiedad, como una presión o dolor en el pecho acompañado de latidos rápidos [3].

Lo que conviene hacer ahora es que tu hijo pare la actividad y descanse, y que lo vea un médico para valorarlo, ya que es importante que un profesional lo revise para asegurarse de que no es nada serio [1][7].

Busca ayuda médica urgente si el dolor es repentino y no desaparece, si se extiende al brazo, el cuello, el estómago o la espalda, o si además tiene sudoración, náuseas, mareo o falta de aire [7].

q: mi hija se desmayo jugando al futbol pero ahora esta bien
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Desmayo haciendo ejercicio, o con palpitaciones o dolor en el pecho: que lo vean en urgencias hoy
text:
El desmayo es una pérdida de conocimiento brusca y corta: suele ocurrir cuando no llega suficiente sangre u oxígeno al cerebro, según la SEUP [1]. Después de un rato de reposo, los niños se recuperan rápido, en un par de minutos [5].

Ahora que está bien, que se incorpore despacio: primero sentada y, tras unos minutos, de pie [5]. Conviene que beba más líquidos, sobre todo cuando hace ejercicio [4]. Si nota que se va a marear otra vez, que se siente o se tumbe de inmediato y respire lento y profundo; si pierde el conocimiento, túmbala con las piernas elevadas y la cabeza de lado [5].

Los desmayos durante el ejercicio físico son uno de los motivos por los que la SEUP recomienda consultar en urgencias [3].

q: cuando se puede empezar con la fruta y la verdura
text: La fruta y la verdura se pueden empezar a ofrecer en torno a los 6 meses, cuando la leche ya no cubre por sí sola las necesidades del bebé y se añaden alimentos complementarios [2]. A partir de ahí, la AEP aconseja introducir progresivamente toda la variedad de frutas y verduras disponible, en cualquiera de las comidas diarias, variando también la forma de presentarlas: trituradas, chafadas o en trozos pequeños [1]. No hay unas frutas mejores que otras para comenzar; la elección depende de los gustos de la familia [1]. Conviene ofrecer los alimentos de uno en uno, con intervalos de unos días, para ver cómo los tolera y los acepta, y sin añadir sal ni azúcar [4]. Durante el primer año, evita las verduras de hoja verde con muchos nitratos, como acelga, espinaca o borraja [1]. Mejor fruta entera que zumo: el zumo no aporta ventajas frente a la fruta y aumenta el riesgo de caries [1].

q: mi hija de 5 años tiene granitos rojos por la tripa que le pican mucho
text:
Los granitos rojos que pican mucho en el cuerpo pueden deberse a la varicela, que empieza con un sarpullido con picor y puede aparecer en cualquier parte del cuerpo, junto con fiebre, dolores y malestar general [6]. También pueden ser urticaria, y en ese caso el farmacéutico puede aconsejar sobre un antihistamínico, aunque puede no ser adecuado en niños pequeños [7].

Mientras tanto, mantén las uñas de la niña cortas y limpias para que no se rasque, y ponle ropa ligera de algodón. Si el picor le impide dormir o está muy incómoda, consulta con tu médico o farmacéutico.

Busca atención urgente si los labios, la boca, la garganta o la lengua se hinchan de repente, si le cuesta respirar o tragar, o si la niña se vuelve muy decaída o no responde como siempre [7].

q: mi hijo es asmatico y se le hunden las costillas al respirar
banner: 🚨 Llama ahora al 112 o acude a urgencias. | Motivo: Dificultad para respirar grave (se marcan las costillas, respira muy rápido, pausas en la respiración, color azulado)
text: El hundimiento de las costillas al respirar (tiraje) es uno de los síntomas de una crisis asmática, según la SEUP [4]. En una crisis asmática, administra de 2 a 4 pulsaciones de salbutamol, aplicadas de una en una, con una cámara espaciadora (y mascarilla facial en niños pequeños), y repite esa dosis a los 10-15 minutos [6]. Mantenlo en reposo, evita el ejercicio y los ambientes con humo o contaminación [6]. Si toma tratamiento de mantenimiento, debe seguir con él durante la crisis [6]. Si la crisis no cede tras el tratamiento en casa, o si te queda alguna duda, acude lo antes posible a un centro sanitario y lleva la cámara espaciadora [6]. La SEUP indica que hay que consultar en urgencias si la dificultad respiratoria empeora, si respira cada vez más deprisa, se le marcan las costillas, mueve mucho el abdomen o se le hunde el pecho [3].

q: y si no le baja la fiebre le puedo dar dalsy
text:
Sí, se puede cambiar al ibuprofeno si el paracetamol no mejora el malestar. Según la SEUP, el paracetamol y el ibuprofeno tienen una eficacia similar y se dan a la dosis recomendada por su pediatra cada 6-8 horas [1]. La AEPap concreta que, si a las 3-4 horas de dar un antitérmico la temperatura sigue alta y el malestar no mejora, es razonable intercambiarlos: si empezó con paracetamol y no mejora, la próxima vez puede dar ibuprofeno [6].

Que la fiebre no baje del todo tras un antitérmico es frecuente y no implica mayor gravedad [3]. El objetivo es el confort del niño, no bajar la fiebre en sí [1]. Asegúrese de que beba abundantes líquidos y no lo abrigue en exceso [1].

Consulte si está decaído, poco reactivo o muy irritable, si le cuesta respirar, si tiene manchas en la piel que no desaparecen al presionarlas, o si no tolera sólidos ni líquidos [7].

banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Signos de deshidratación: ojos hundidos, orina poco, boca seca, vómitos persistentes o diarrea abundante >24 h

q: mi hijo tiene diarrea pero quiere comer normal
text: La gastroenteritis suele mejorar por sí sola, con reposo y abundantes líquidos y electrolitos [5]. Lo más importante es evitar la deshidratación: ofrécele soluciones de rehidratación oral ya preparadas, en dosis pequeñas y tomas frecuentes, y la cantidad que te hayan indicado después de cada deposición líquida o cada vómito [3]. No uses soluciones caseras ni refrescos comerciales para reponer las pérdidas [2]. No le des medicamentos para la diarrea o los vómitos sin consultar con su pediatra [2]. Consulta lo antes posible si el niño está irritable o con menos energía, si la diarrea dura más de un día, si tiene fiebre, si las deposiciones son muy frecuentes, si hay signos de deshidratación como sed, boca seca, orinar menos o no mojar los pañales durante 3 horas o más, o si hay sangre o pus en las heces [1].

q: mi hijo tiene manchas despues de tener fiebre, puede ser por la fiebre?
text:
Si el bebé tiene menos de 3 meses, la fiebre necesita que lo vea un médico el mismo día [2].

En un niño mayor, las manchas rojas en la piel que no desaparecen al presionarlas son un signo de alarma: hay que consultar en urgencias [2]. Si las manchas sí desaparecen al presionar, la SEUP las incluye entre los motivos para pedir consulta con el pediatra, no para urgencias [3]. La fiebre suele durar entre 2 y 4 días, y puede durar más sin que eso signifique mayor gravedad [1].

Mientras tanto, vigila su estado general y que tenga buen color, y fíjate en si aparecen petequias, esos puntos rojos que no se borran al apretar en sus laterales [1]. Ofrécele líquidos a menudo y en pequeñas cantidades; si no tolera ni sólidos ni líquidos, hay que consultar [2]. La dosis de antitérmico depende de la edad y el peso, así que consúltala con tu pediatra [1].

¿Qué edad tiene? Con la edad afino la respuesta.

q: mi hijo tiene 2 años y 39 de fiebre desde ayer, le doy Apiretal?
text: Con 39 de fiebre, lo primero es tratar el malestar del niño, no la fiebre en sí: el objetivo es su confort, según la SEUP [1]. Puede darle paracetamol (Apiretal) a la dosis que le haya recomendado su pediatra, cada 6-8 horas [1]. No hace falta alternarlo con ibuprofeno cada 3-4 horas salvo que el niño esté incómodo antes de las 6 horas [1]. Asegúrese de que beba abundantes líquidos y no lo fuerce a comer si no tiene apetito [1]. No lo bañe en agua fría ni le ponga paños húmedos: resulta desagradable y no baja la fiebre [1]. Es normal que la fiebre dure entre 2 y 4 días, y que no baje del todo tras el antitérmico [4]. Consulte en urgencias si está decaído, poco reactivo o muy irritable, si le cuesta respirar, si no tolera líquidos ni sólidos o si le salen manchas en la piel que no desaparecen al presionarlas [7].

q: mi bebe tiene muchos mocos y le cuesta dormir
text:
Los mocos y la tos son lo habitual en un catarro de vías altas, una infección vírica de nariz y garganta muy frecuente en los primeros años, según la SEUP [3]. La mucosidad puede durar hasta una semana [4].

Para que duerma mejor, hazle lavados nasales antes de las tomas y antes de dormir, preferiblemente con suero salino y nunca con agua del grifo [4]. Ofrécele líquidos abundantes y no le fuerces a comer si no tiene ganas [4]. Mantenlo lejos del humo y de lugares donde se fume [4]. No uses anticatarrales, mucolíticos, descongestivos ni jarabes para la tos, sobre todo si es menor de 6 años [4]. Si tiene fiebre por encima de 38 ºC y está incómodo, dale el antitérmico que le recomiende habitualmente su pediatra [4].

Consulta a tu pediatra si le cuesta respirar, respira más deprisa, está irritable o le cuesta comer [5].

q: puedo darle Apiretal despues de las vacunas
text: Sí, se puede dar paracetamol (Apiretal) después de las vacunas para aliviar el dolor o bajar la fiebre, según el Gobierno de Canadá [1]. Tras la vacuna MenB, el NHS recomienda dar paracetamol al bebé: una dosis lo antes posible después de vacunar, una segunda a las 4-6 horas, y una tercera 4-6 horas después, dejando al menos 4 horas entre dosis y sin pasar de 4 dosis en 24 horas [4]. La dosis depende del peso del niño; puedes usar la calculadora de PediBot para paracetamol e ibuprofeno. Las reacciones leves (fiebre, dolor en la zona, irritabilidad, somnolencia) son normales y desaparecen solas en horas o pocos días [1]. Consulta a tu médico si la fiebre alta continúa más de 48 horas tras la vacuna, o si lo ves decaído y te preocupa [4].

q: mi hijo se ha tragado una pila de boton

text: La ingestión de una pila de botón es una urgencia: la batería puede quemar el esófago en pocas horas, según la SEUP [5]. No le provoques el vómito ni le des agua, leche, aceite ni ningún alimento [3]. Si tiene algo sólido en la boca, se ve y está accesible, quítaselo, pero nunca a ciegas [3]. Intenta determinar cuántas y de qué tamaño se ha tragado [3]. Una pila de botón alojada en el esófago debe extraerse con urgencia [5]. Mientras llega la ayuda, sepáralo de la pila y vigila que respire bien y tenga buen color [3].

q: mi bebe tiene menos pañales mojados hoy
banner: 🚨 Con estos síntomas hay que acudir a urgencias hoy, sin esperar. | Motivo: Signos de deshidratación: ojos hundidos, orina poco, boca seca, vómitos persistentes o diarrea abundante >24 h

La deshidratación puede ser leve o grave, y los bebés tienen más probabilidades de deshidratarse [3][7].

Lo más importante ahora es reponer los líquidos con solución de rehidratación oral ya preparada, no con soluciones caseras ni refrescos comerciales [4]. Ofrézcasela en pequeñas cantidades y con frecuencia, respetando su apetito, y mantenga la lactancia materna normal o incluso más a menudo si la pide [1]. No hace falta ayunar ni evitar los lácteos [1].

Busque ayuda médica de inmediato si además hay confusión, desmayo, falta de micción, latidos o respiración rápidos [3].

q: mi hijo tiene tos pero no le cuesta respirar
text:
La tos sin dificultad para respirar es uno de los síntomas del catarro de vías altas, una infección vírica de nariz y garganta muy frecuente en los primeros años [6]. Es normal que tengan entre 6 y 8 catarros al año, incluso más si va a la guardería [6].

En casa, vigila su estado general y la aparición de dificultad para respirar: que se le marquen las costillas o se le hunda el pecho, que respire rápido o se fatigue al caminar o correr, o dolor en el pecho al respirar [2]. Ofrécele líquidos y, si tiene fiebre, los antitérmicos habituales [4].

Consulta en urgencias si empeora su estado general, está decaído, somnoliento o muy irritable, o si aparece dificultad para respirar [2].

Que un bebé moje menos el pañal es una señal de deshidratación: en bebés y niños pequeños, no mojar los pañales durante 3 horas o más es un signo de alarma, según MedlinePlus [4]. La gastroenteritis puede causar deshidratación, y los bebés tienen mayor riesgo [2].
